original.target_description: Published Schmeichel (2007), Experiment 1, pp. 243–244: attention-control versus no-control conditions; operation-span and sentence-span performance standardized within test type and analyzed together. Page 244 reports four separate recall endpoints plus distractor performance and a manipulation check. The supplied description and page locator do not uniquely identify one outcome/test.

replication.target_description: Lurquin et al. (2016), p. 12 inspected in full: includes first-versus-second-half OSPAN performance, condition × task-half interaction, and several motivation/effort condition contrasts. The broad executive-control description and study identifier do not uniquely identify which p. 12 test is assigned.

n.sample_role: Participants with usable complete datasets in the full-sample OSPAN condition comparison; 100 per randomized condition.
n.exclusions: 202 collected; two excluded: one did not complete final questions because of experimenter error; one had 76% equation-verification accuracy, below the 80% criterion. No exclusions for guessing a hypothesis, dishonest responding, or non-native English.
n.location: Method, Participants, final paragraph; Results opening paragraph establishes full-sample Hypothesis 1 test.
n.quote: Therefore, we collected data from a total of 202 participants leaving us with 200 usable datasets (100 in each condition).

es.location: Results, Hypothesis 1: Group-Level Ego-Depletion Effect, first paragraph (HTML canonical text; Fig 1)

p.location: Results, Hypothesis 1: Group-Level Ego-Depletion Effect, first paragraph (HTML canonical text; Fig 1)

reported_success.quote: we still see no evidence of ego-depletion.

notes:
Replication paper is available and title verified. Page 12 contains multiple tests, including OSPAN time-on-task and its interaction (printed partial eta-squared), and motivation/effort contrasts (printed d). The supplied locator does not identify a target among these tests; no test was selected based on input order or desired metric. The page-11 overall condition contrast was not silently substituted. Reported success is the authors’ overall ego-depletion verdict, not an inferred significance classification.
Source follow-up: Fresh original-only blind validation. Published article title, author, year, journal and DOI verified against supplied primary source. Source version: published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service. Original source: /home/lukas/.t3/worktrees/fred-data/audit-fred-stats-2026-10/audit/fred_stats_2026-10/texts/followup_mac_32fd76ba5dde685e762284a3.txt. PDF cross-check: /home/lukas/work/fred-mac-recovery-20261030/private_batch_01/artifacts/32fd76ba5dde685e762284a3_ebsco_psycinfo.pdf. Experiment 1 Method (p. 243) identifies a final sample of 141 undergraduate participants after excluding four who tried to memorize distracting words; this sample applies to the combined recall analyses. However, p. 244 separately reports individual-word recall, correctly recalled sets, total words in correctly recalled sets, and longest correctly recalled set, each with its own F, p and d. The input does not identify which of these endpoints is assigned; no test was selected from input order, requested metric, or replication reference. Statistic fields remain null because a unique test cannot be established. The supplied broad description also mentions reverse digit span and response inhibition, which are not the Experiment 1 recall outcomes. No original statistics were taken from replication sources. Reported success and replication were not assessed because target_side is original.
